subject: Elastic seat rollover and feature tradeoffs for Medilane
messages:
From: Jill Park <procurement@medilane.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: aaron.tsao@medilane.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question — rollover and feature bundling

Hi Karthik,

Quick packaging question as we finalize numbers for Q3: Medilane is trying to reconcile two needs — a small pool of committed seats for predictable unit economics, plus an elastic burst model for month-to-month spikes (surg centers). Our procurement team is also asking if unused committed seats can roll over into the next quarter or convert into credits.

What we’d like to understand from Redwood:
- Can committed seats be converted to credits for one quarter without penalty?
- Is there a way to mix an annual seat commit with a metered burst bucket and have usage fall back to the commit first?
- Any recommended feature-bundling that avoids paying for the full enterprise bundle while retaining the integrations we need (SOC2 logs + advanced tracing)?

We’re on a tight cadence — budget signoff next Friday. If you can share a short note with options and any pricing delta, that’d be helpful.

Thanks,
Jill Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Medilane Health
attachments: (none)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jill Park <procurement@medilane.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — rollover and feature bundling

Hi Jill — thanks for the clear ask. Short version up front: yes, we can cover both patterns and offer limited rollover/crediting with an annual commit plus an elastic burst bucket. Details below and attached a proposal with line-item pricing (Medilane_proposal_v3.pdf).

Option A — Annual seat commit + elastic burst
- Commit: 100 seats, annual prepay (15% discount on list for 12-mo commit)
- Burst: Metered pool (pay-as-you-go) for spikes; routed to burst after commit is exhausted each month
- Rollover: Unused commit hours convert to credits usable in Q1 of the following year, capped at 20% of annual commit value
- Feature access: SOC2 audit logs + tracing included on commit; advanced telemetry retention add-on available at reduced rate

Option B — Quarterly commit with flexible conversion
- Commit: quarterly prepay, smaller discount (7%)
- Rollover: unused seats convert to short-term credits valid 30–90 days depending on tier

Tradeoffs and recommended configuration
- If predictability is primary, go annual commit (Option A) — better unit economics and included telemetry features.
- If burst volatility is high, add a larger metered burst pool (we can set a soft floor so burst charges never exceed X% of commit cost).

Next steps
1) I attached a tailored pricing worksheet (Medilane_proposal_v3.pdf).
2) If this aligns, we’ll drop in amended MAA language for the rollover credit cap (see draft Redwood_MAA_draft.docx).
3) Ben — can you confirm whether we can increase the rollover cap to 25% for strategic customers?

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk numbers.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
attachments: Medilane_proposal_v3.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jill Park <procurement@medilane.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — rollover and feature bundling

Karthik — quick thoughts:
- We can be flexible on the rollover cap for an account of this size. I’m comfortable with 25% cap if they sign 12-month commit >= $120k ARR, and we add a 3-month notice for downsizing.
- For feature bundling: include SOC2 logs + 90-day trace retention in the commit. Charge for longer retention as an optional add-on.
- Discount: move to 18% on the annual commit if they also agree to a one-time onboarding fee of $12k (covers dedicated telemetry ingest + connectors).

Jill — to make this simple for procurement, we can draft two rows in the proposal: "Core commit (incl. SOC2 & tracing)" and "Elastic burst bucket (metered)" with an example month showing how commit exhausts before burst billing.

—Ben
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference
attachments: (none)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: Jill Park <procurement@medilane.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging question — rollover and feature bundling

Adding a quick operational note: if Medilane needs seat pooling across multiple org units we should add a clause for seat portability (internal transfers) and make the rollover credits non-transferable outside the legal entity. Also suggest:
- Pilot: 30-day pilot with 20 seats free trial credits on the burst bucket to validate surge patterns.
- If pilot shows >30% monthly volatility, automatic recommendation to increase burst bucket with a 1-mo lookback policy.

Jill — would you take pilot + 25% rollover cap + 18% discount + $12k onboarding as acceptable for procurement signoff? If yes, we’ll prepare the MAA and get DocuSign ready.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Packaging question — rollover and feature bundling

Karthik / Lauren / Ben — thanks, this is exactly the clarity we needed. Medilane leadership is comfortable with the following as the path to sign:
- 12‑month commit at 100 seats
- 18% annual discount, $12k onboarding fee
- 25% rollover cap into next fiscal quarter (non-transferable)
- Pilot: 30-day burst credits (20 seats) to validate surges
- Include SOC2 logs + 90‑day trace retention in core commit

Please send the MAA and DocuSign link; procurement will process as soon as the contract is in DocuSign.

Jill Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Medilane Health
